meta.title: Testing rovers on Earth vs on the Moon: what one test costs
meta.question: How much does NASA save by testing prototypes such as rovers and other hardware on Earth, compared with what it would cost to test them on the Moon?
meta.answer_in_one_line: Scenario-based: delivering a prototype to the Moon costs hundreds of times (11 kg rover) to tens of thousands of times (larger rovers) one Earth field campaign; the Moon side counts only the delivery.
scope_includes: Moon: delivery to the lunar surface only (mass x CLPS price per kg), with and without landing risk; DSN as a separate accounting line
Earth: one 6-person field campaign from Malaga at official rates (per diem, travel, freight, 4x4s, fees); NASA facility agreements per test-week as an order of magnitude
scope_excludes: Salaries, insurance, customs, the prototype itself
A like-for-like test: Earth analogs do not reproduce lunar gravity, vacuum, dust and thermal conditions together
meta.money_rule: Amounts kept in source currency and year, converted at the end; nominal in the base case. Inflation variant (Spain HICP for EUR, US CPI IMF relay for USD) is a sensitivity only.

labels.OFFICIAL: a rate or statistic a government body issues as its own figure
labels.PUBLISHED: a value printed by a named, dated source (company, press, paper, or an estimate in a government report)
labels.DERIVED: our own arithmetic on OFFICIAL or PUBLISHED inputs
labels.ILLUSTRATIVE: a team assumption used only to show the method

meta.not_built: Fidelity-vs-cost Pareto frontier (M3): similarity scores do not exist yet.

flags.LOWER_BOUND_MOON: Moon side counts only the delivery to the surface: flight hardware, qualification, integration, operations staff and launch-slot risk are not included, so it is a lower bound on the whole cost of a lunar test (not on the delivery price itself, see LINEAR_PER_KG).
flags.LINEAR_PER_KG: Assumes the price per kg of a 75-94 kg CLPS manifest scales linearly to the payload mass. For a small rover (11 kg) this assumes a shared ride on someone else's lander; a dedicated delivery costs a whole task order. For a large rover it overstates: VIPER's own delivery contracts imply a lower price per kg.
flags.OIG_ESTIMATE: The OIG price per kg is an estimate from 2023 task-order prices, not a price list.
flags.LANDING_PRIOR: Landing-success probability uses a declared Beta prior on 13 attempts (2019 to 14 Nov 2026).
flags.AS_OF_DATE: Mission-outcome tallies are as of 2026-11-14 per NASA, CNSA and ISRO pages.
flags.DSN_ACCOUNTING: DSN aperture fees are full-cost accounting charges (2022 rate), not cash paid by a NASA mission; shown separately, never added to cash costs.
flags.WEATHER_GENERIC: Workable-day fraction is a generic ILLUSTRATIVE range for every site in the base case: the station data are confidence low.
flags.WEATHER_STATION_LOW: Sensitivity uses station-based workable days (rain and cold only, wind not evaluated): an upper bound, confidence low.
flags.WIND_ILLUSTRATIVE: Wind losses are an ILLUSTRATIVE range (no wind data near the sites).
flags.WEATHER_NO_DATA: No weather station within 75 km (Atacama, Holuhraun): ILLUSTRATIVE workable-day range.
flags.PER_DIEM_NOMINAL: Spanish per diems are nominal 2002 (abroad) and 2005 (Spain) amounts still in force, not market prices; about 0.3-0.5x US rates abroad.
flags.EU_TRAVEL_FLAT_RATE: Travel uses EU flat-rate contributions per participant (return trip, by one-way distance band), not airfares.
flags.SEASONALITY_SPAIN_PROXY: Seasonal swing of lodging and travel taken from Spain HICP (2025 months), also applied abroad.
flags.CORRELATION_DECLARED: Rank correlation between travel and lodging is a declared assumption.
flags.FREIGHT_MARKUP_ILLUSTRATIVE: Air freight = index spot rate times an ILLUSTRATIVE small-shipment markup (no lane quote captured).
flags.DG_SURCHARGE_ILLUSTRATIVE: Dangerous-goods surcharge for lithium batteries is an ILLUSTRATIVE range (none published; battery content unknown).
flags.ROAD_MILEAGE_PROXY: Road freight is the official mileage allowance times the round-trip road distance (own-car proxy, not a van hire or haulage quote).
flags.VEHICLE_RATE_ILLUSTRATIVE: 4x4 rental per day is an ILLUSTRATIVE range scaled by the Eurostat price level; no rental rate was captured.
flags.PLI_MISSING: No Eurostat price level for Chile: vehicle rate left at the EU27 level.
flags.PERMIT_FEE_NOT_PUBLISHED: Authorisation required, fee not published: counted as zero.
flags.PERMIT_AUTHORITY_UNVERIFIED: The permitting authority or rules for this site could not be confirmed (audit: confidence low).
flags.MDRS_FEE_LODGING_OVERLAP: MDRS crew fee may already include habitat lodging that the per diem also counts (upper side).
flags.OFFROAD_LAST_LEG: Site lies off the road network: routing ends at the nearest road, the last leg is not costed.
flags.HOLUHRAUN_SEASONAL_TRACK: Holuhraun is reached on the F910 highland track, summer only; drive times understated.
flags.AIRPORT_CHOICE_LOW_TIME: Airport chosen by a drive time the audit rates low (F-road).
flags.CUSTOMS_NOT_INCLUDED: Customs, ATA carnet, insurance, salaries and the prototype itself are not included on the Earth side.
flags.CAMPAIGN_SIZE: Campaign size (6 people, 10 test days, 2 travel days, 400 kg kit) is an ILLUSTRATIVE team default.
flags.FACILITY_ORDER_OF_MAGNITUDE: NASA facility agreements are multi-year reimbursable estimates for non-rover partners; per-test-week values are an order of magnitude, not a price per rover test.
flags.VOI_ILLUSTRATIVE: Value-of-information inputs (prior, redesign cost, test sensitivity and specificity) are ILLUSTRATIVE.
flags.INFLATION_SENSITIVITY: Inflation-adjusted variant (Spain HICP for EUR, US CPI IMF relay for USD), sensitivity only.
flags.INFLATION_GAP: No annual price index for the amount's year: left nominal in the inflation variant.
flags.LOW_CONF_SENSITIVITY: Uses confidence-low rows; labelled sensitivity only, never the base case.
flags.NOT_SOURCED: This variant is not supported by a captured source sentence (audit).

headlines.title: Earth field campaigns paid for by one lunar delivery (174 kg rover)
headlines.includes: Moon: delivery price only (mass x CLPS price per kg, assumed linear in mass). Earth: travel, per diem, freight, 4x4s and fees of one 6-person campaign from Malaga carrying the kit plus the rover, P50.
headlines.excludes: Flight hardware, qualification, operations, launch, salaries, insurance, customs, the prototype itself.
headlines.allowed_sentence: If CLPS prices per kg scale linearly with mass, delivering a 174 kg rover to the Moon costs about EUR 220 M (P10-P90 EUR 164-307 M), counting the delivery only; at the median that equals about 3,600 (Mars Desert Research Station (Hanksville Utah)) to 17,000 (Tabernas Desert (Almeria) and Rio Tinto - Pena de Hierro headwaters (Huelva), a tie) one-off Earth field campaigns at official rates.
headlines.must_not_mean: Not a saving NASA has booked, and not a like-for-like test: Earth analogs do not reproduce lunar gravity, vacuum, dust and thermal conditions together. Earth tests reduce risk before flight; they do not replace it.

headlines.title: Moon delivery cost of one test, by rover size (P50)
headlines.includes: Mass x price per kg (triangular over the six audited figures), assumed linear in mass.
headlines.excludes: Everything except the delivery to the surface (hardware, operations, launch-slot risk).
headlines.allowed_sentence: Delivery alone (P50), if the CLPS price per kg scales linearly with mass: about EUR 14 M for an 11 kg rover (assumes a shared ride; a whole CLPS task order was $77.5-180.4 M at award), EUR 220 M for 174 kg, and EUR 599 M for a VIPER-class 475 kg rover. For the largest class linear scaling overstates the delivery: NASA's actual VIPER delivery contracts were $190-323 M (nominal USD).
headlines.must_not_mean: Not a price quote and not a lower bound on the delivery itself; it assumes the price per kg scales linearly with mass. It is a lower bound only on the whole cost of a lunar test, which also needs hardware and operations.

headlines.title: One field campaign on Earth (P50, cheapest to dearest site)
headlines.includes: Spanish official per diem (RD 462/2002), EU flat-rate travel contribution, equipment freight, 2 4x4s, published permit and site fees; 6 people, 10 workable test days, 2 travel days.
headlines.excludes: Salaries, insurance, customs, the prototype, contingency; market prices (official rates are used). At MDRS the crew fee may overlap with lodging.
headlines.allowed_sentence: At official Spanish rates, one 6-person field campaign from Malaga costs about EUR 13k (Tabernas Desert (Almeria) and Rio Tinto - Pena de Hierro headwaters (Huelva), a tie) to EUR 57k (Mars Desert Research Station (Hanksville Utah)) at the median (P10-P90 EUR 12k-78k across sites).
headlines.must_not_mean: Not a market price or a budget quote. Sites inside one tier (see charts.site_costs.rank_tiers) cannot be told apart; with US government per diem rates the order of the overseas sites changes.

headlines.title: Price to deliver 1 kg to the lunar surface
headlines.includes: Four CLPS award prices / planned NASA payload mass (same release) and the two OIG estimates.
headlines.excludes: Task-order growth after award; the Firefly far-side mass (includes an orbital relay).
headlines.allowed_sentence: Award price divided by planned NASA payload mass, at selection, ranges from about $0.84 M to $2.41 M per kg; the NASA OIG estimated that CLPS deliveries cost about $1.2 million per kg, based on 2023 task-order prices (NASA's 2019 estimate: about $1 million).
headlines.must_not_mean: An estimate, not a price list; not the price of a kg on the Moon today.

headlines.title: 1 kg to the Moon vs 1 kg of air cargo
headlines.includes: OIG estimate ($1.2 M/kg, 2023) divided by the Xeneta global average air-cargo spot rate (3.13 USD/kg, 2026-08).
headlines.allowed_sentence: The NASA OIG's estimate of about $1.2 million per kg for CLPS deliveries (based on 2023 task-order prices) is about 380,000 times the Xeneta global average air-cargo spot rate for August 2026 (3.13 USD/kg).
headlines.must_not_mean: Not a price list on either side; the air rate is a global average spot rate, not a specific lane.

headlines.title: Lunar landing attempts that fully succeeded, 2019-01-01 to 2026-11-14
headlines.includes: 13 landing attempts (craft that never tried to land excluded).
headlines.allowed_sentence: Of 13 lunar landing attempts from 2019 to 14 November 2026, 5 fully succeeded, 3 landed but tipped over or ended early, and 5 failed (our classification of agency and operator statements; JAXA counts SLIM as a success).
headlines.must_not_mean: Do not say 'to date' without the date; do not merge partial into success.

headlines.title: Delivery cost per SUCCESSFUL test vs the delivery price
headlines.includes: Beta posterior on full successes: strict Beta(6,9), mean 0.40; operator claims Beta(7,8), mean 0.47; uniform prior.
headlines.excludes: Partial landings count as not successful; no learning curve over time.
headlines.allowed_sentence: Allowing for landing failures, the delivery cost per fully successful landing is about 2.1-2.5 times the delivery price (median; the mean is 2.3-2.8 times), from 13 lunar landing attempts between 2019 and 14 November 2026 with a uniform prior.
headlines.must_not_mean: Not a forecast for a specific lander; a statistical summary of recent attempts.

headlines.title: What NASA contracted to deliver VIPER
headlines.includes: TO-20A initial (June 2020), December 2021 and February 2024 values (OIG); CS-7 2025 potential value (NASA).
headlines.excludes: VIPER itself (about $500 M, OIG, January 2024, not counting delivery).
headlines.allowed_sentence: NASA's VIPER delivery task order (TO-20A) was priced at $199.5 M in June 2020 and $322.8 M by February 2024 (OIG); in 2025 NASA ordered a new delivery (CS-7, Blue Origin) with a total potential value of $190 M. VIPER itself cost about $500 million (OIG, January 2024), not counting its delivery.
headlines.must_not_mean: Never add these figures to each other; never add $505.4 M and $500 M (same fact).

headlines.title: NASA's own Earth test-facility agreements (value of a whole multi-year agreement)
headlines.includes: JSC Building 353 vacuum-chamber agreement with Sandia and KSC GMRO regolith / 1-6 g offload agreement with ProtoInnovations (2024 reimbursable Space Act Agreements, estimated totals).
headlines.excludes: Rover hardware, staff, the partner's own costs. A split per test-week exists only in facility_per_test.csv as an order of magnitude.
headlines.allowed_sentence: NASA's own reimbursable agreements price a year of vacuum-chamber or regolith-lab testing in the $0.7-1.2 M range for a whole multi-year agreement.
headlines.must_not_mean: Not the cost of testing a rover and not a price per test; the partners are not rover programmes, and these facilities do not reproduce lunar gravity, vacuum, dust and thermal conditions together.

headlines.title: DSN accounting charge for a 100-day VIPER-class surface test
headlines.includes: 100 days x 8-24 antenna-hours per day (ILLUSTRATIVE) x $1,792 per hour x AW 1 x MW 1 (single 34 m antenna, uplink and downlink).
headlines.excludes: Mission operations staff; any cash outlay.
headlines.allowed_sentence: NASA charges missions about $1,792 per antenna-hour (2022 accounting rate); for a 100-day surface test that is an accounting charge of roughly $1.8-3.1 M.
headlines.must_not_mean: It is not cash paid and not a current price; never added to the delivery cost.

headlines.title: Spanish official per diem vs US rate abroad
headlines.includes: RD 462/2002 Group 2 (2002/2005 nominal) vs US State Dept 2026 maximum rates at the same places.
headlines.excludes: US sites (there the two are about equal).
headlines.allowed_sentence: At the Spanish, Chilean and Icelandic sites, the Spanish official per diem, Group 2 (RD 462/2002), is about 0.3-0.5 times the US State Department rate for the same place (November 2026 table); it is a nominal 2002 (abroad) or 2005 (Spain) amount still in force, not a market price.
headlines.must_not_mean: Do not call the Spanish amounts current market costs.

headlines.title: What moves the Earth cost most
headlines.includes: Tornado: each input from its P10 to its P90 with the others at P50 (base case).
headlines.allowed_sentence: At 7 of 9 sites the input that moves the campaign cost most is: Workable-day fraction (generic, ILLUSTRATIVE).
headlines.must_not_mean: The ranking follows from declared ranges; it is not measured.

headlines.title: Value of testing a 174 kg rover first in a well-matched analog (ILLUSTRATIVE)
headlines.includes: L = Moon delivery P50 ($243 M), R = 20% of L, prior defect probability 0.15, s and c by fidelity (all ILLUSTRATIVE).
headlines.excludes: Any measured defect rate; the hardware cost of a mid-size rover (none published).
headlines.allowed_sentence: In the illustrative value-of-information tree, testing first in a well-matched analog is worth about $20.6 M (generic analog $10.4 M, ceiling $29.1 M), against a campaign of tens of thousands of euros.
headlines.must_not_mean: Nothing here is measured: p, s, c and R are invented to show the method.

headlines.title: Fixing an error in operations vs in test (Stecklein 2004)
headlines.includes: Abstract summary factors: test 21-78x, operations 29-1,500x the requirements-phase cost.
headlines.excludes: Any specific rover; any money amount.
headlines.allowed_sentence: NASA cost data (Stecklein et al. 2004) put a requirements error found in test at 21-78 times, and in operations at 29-1,500 times, the cost of fixing it in the requirements phase; so an error found in operations instead of test costs about 1.4-19 times more (same end of the ranges), and one found in test instead of design about 7-10 times more.
headlines.must_not_mean: Not a measured multiple for lunar rovers.

headlines.title: Mars landed elements that fully succeeded, as of 2026-11-14
headlines.includes: Each Deep Space 2 probe counted as one element.
headlines.allowed_sentence: Of 18 Mars landed elements (1971 to 2026-11-14), 10 fully succeeded, 1 partially and 7 failed (counted by element, DS2 = 2).
headlines.must_not_mean: Counted by element, not by mission; say so.

headlines.title: Exchange rate used
headlines.includes: All USD amounts; nominal, not inflated (base case).
headlines.allowed_sentence: Converted at the ECB reference rate on 2026-11-13: 1.1052 USD per EUR.

voi.about:
M4: value of information of an analog test before flight (plan 7.3, model 4).

Tree: fly as is, or test first and redesign if the test fails. L = loss if a terrain defect ends
the mission, R = redesign and delay cost, p = prior probability of the defect, s = sensitivity
(the test finds a real defect), c = specificity (no false alarm). A redesign removes the defect.

  no information:     E0   = min(p L, R)                 (fly as is, or always redesign)
  perfect information: EVPI = E0 - p min(L, R)
  one analog test:    P+ = s p + (1 - c)(1 - p);  p+ = s p / P+;  p- = (1 - s) p / (1 - P+)
                      E1 = P+ min(p+ L, R) + (1 - P+) min(p- L, R)
                      EVSI = E0 - E1   (0 <= EVSI <= EVPI)
  net value = EVSI - campaign cost (M1, converted to USD)

L per mass class = Moon delivery cost (M6, P50) + published hardware cost where one exists (VIPER
project cost, OIG, January 2024). R = fraction of L. p, s, c and the fraction are ILLUSTRATIVE.
Can claim: the value rises with fidelity and never exceeds EVPI; the order of magnitude against a
campaign cost. Cannot claim: anything measured; linking site similarity to s is an assumption.
voi.units: USD (nominal; Moon side in USD because its sources are USD)
voi.label: ILLUSTRATIVE
